name: Westminster
description: The political and royal nerve centre of the United Kingdom, where grand neo-Gothic monuments, royal parks, and stately government avenues line the historic banks of the Thames.
what_famous_for: Big Ben, the Houses of Parliament, Westminster Abbey, and Buckingham Palace.
insider_tip: Walk through Victoria Tower Gardens along the river embankment for an uncrowded view of Parliament's ornate Victoria Tower.

name: Covent Garden
description: A sensory feast of cobbled plazas, world-class street performance, the Royal Opera House, and designer shopping, connecting seamlessly to colourful micro-sanctuaries like Neal's Yard.
what_famous_for: The Apple Market, West End theatres, street performers, and vibrant dining.
insider_tip: Slip into Floral Street and Rose Street to discover quiet 17th-century historic pubs tucked away from the main piazza.

name: Soho & Chinatown
description: London's most vibrant entertainment and dining labyrinth, celebrated for jazz basements, heritage Italian coffee bars, indie theatre, and Chinatown's bustling dumpling houses.
what_famous_for: Legendary music history, eclectic global cuisine, Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club, and Chinatown.
insider_tip: Visit Kingly Court, a three-storey open-air courtyard packed with independent food concepts that hums with energy day and night.

name: Notting Hill
description: An enchanting West London neighbourhood of pastel Victorian townhouses, cobblestone mews, antique treasure troves, and stylish independent cafés.
what_famous_for: Portobello Road Market, pastel stucco terraces, and Europe's largest carnival.
insider_tip: Wander through St Luke's Mews and Lancaster Road for the most picturesque pastel street compositions in the city.

name: Camden Town
description: London's rock-and-roll heartland, where alternative subcultures, vintage clothing emporiums, live gig venues, and global street food gather around the Regent's Canal locks.
what_famous_for: Camden Stables Market, punk and indie music heritage, and canal lockside dining.
insider_tip: Board a waterbus along Regent's Canal from Camden Lock to Little Venice for a magical low-key journey through the heart of London Zoo.

name: Greenwich
description: A riverside UNESCO World Heritage maritime village where royal architecture, naval history, timekeeping heritage, and sweeping hilltop vistas converge.
what_famous_for: Prime Meridian of the world (GMT), Cutty Sark clipper, Old Royal Naval College, and panoramic park views.
insider_tip: Arrive via river boat from Westminster Pier and return via the Greenwich Foot Tunnel under the Thames to Island Gardens for great photography.

name: South Bank & Bankside
description: A continuous, pedestrianised riverside promenade buzzing with cultural institutions, skateboarders, street food stalls, river views, and illuminated bridges.
what_famous_for: The London Eye, Tate Modern, Shakespeare's Globe, and panoramic Thames boardwalks.
insider_tip: Walk the illuminated riverside path at twilight between the National Theatre and Millennium Bridge to see the City skyline glow across the river.

name: Shoreditch & East End
description: The creative epicenter of East London, transformed from industrial textile warehouses into an open-air street art gallery with vintage markets and 24-hour bagel shops.
what_famous_for: Street art murals, Brick Lane curry houses, vintage fashion markets, and indie tech culture.
insider_tip: Explore Redchurch Street for high-end indie concept stores and artisanal chocolate tasting before heading down Brick Lane.
